From: Anika Patel <anika@healthbridge.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-14T15:12:00Z
Subject: HealthBridge DPA v3 — SCCs & role mapping

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Attached is our current DPA (HealthBridge_DPA_v3.pdf) with embedded redlines (HB_DPA_redlines_from_hb_v1.docx). The two items our legal/compliance team flagged as blockers for signature are: 1) explicit controller/processor role mapping across the MSA + Order Form; 2) confirmation of which SCCs template Redwood will rely on and how transfer addenda are handled; and 3) KMS / key custody controls and whether HSM-backed KMS is available for EU workloads.

We also attached a short procurement checklist and would like to align on whether the order form needs an explicit Data Residency clause (we're in Amsterdam and need EU-only processing for certain datasets). Can your legal/product folks propose concrete language for the role mapping and a short statement on SCCs?

Would you be available for a 30-minute call early next week (Mon/Tue)? Tom from procurement (cc'd) will join.

Best,
Anika Patel
Head of Privacy & Compliance
HealthBridge

Anika — thanks for the DPA and the clear callouts. Looping in Laura (legal) and Aditya (privacy) so we can put proposed language on paper before the call.

Quick read: three things we'd like to propose in advance of a call so Tom/Procurement can see where we land:
- Role mapping: Redwood proposes to be Processor for all inference API processing, and Controller only for telemetry/aggregated usage reports; we will draft explicit Order Form language that pins processing scopes to named datasets.
- SCCs: Redwood relies on the latest EU Commission SCCs for processor-to-processor/transfers and will adopt the recommended clauses; Laura will provide the exact recital we prefer. We propose a Transfer Addendum approach if the customer needs additional contractual safeguards for specific sub-processor routes.
- KMS/HSM: we can offer KMS integration with customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for Dedicated/Private deployments; for hosted plans we offer HSM-backed key storage in our EU region — we'll spell the operational evidence we can provide (KMS logs, key rotation cadence).

I've attached a short set of redline suggestions (redlines_steph_20270714.pdf) that reconcile our MSA/Order Form tie-outs with the DPA redlines you sent. Can you confirm which datasets must remain EU-only? That will determine whether we add an explicit residency clause to the Order Form or handle it as an SLO in the DPA.

Monday 10:00–12:00Z or Tuesday 14:00–16:00Z works for our side.

Thanks — Stephanie

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-07-16T14:20:00Z
Subject: RE: HealthBridge DPA v3 — SCCs & role mapping

Hi Anika / team — I reviewed HealthBridge_DPA_v3 and HB redlines and drafted positions. High level: we can accept most of HealthBridge's redlines but need to tighten a few points to preserve standard processor obligations. Proposed edits attached (DPA_markup_LB.docx). Key positions below and suggested language to insert into the DPA / MSA tie-out:

1) Controller / Processor allocation (proposed insertion into MSA order-form annex):
"For the avoidance of doubt, Customer is the Controller for Customer Data and Redwood is a Processor that processes Customer Data solely on Customer's documented instructions as set forth in the Order Form and DPA. Redwood will not process Customer Data for its own purposes except as expressly authorized in writing. Telemetry and aggregated usage metrics do not constitute Customer Data under this DPA."

2) SCCs and transfer mechanism: reference the EU Commission SCCs for controller-processor and processor-processor flows. Suggested recital: "Where data transfers outside the EEA are required, the Parties agree to rely on the EU Commission standard contractual clauses in force at the time of transfer, and to adopt a Transfer Addendum describing the specific transfer routes and supplementary technical measures where required by applicable law."

3) Subprocessor notification and approval window: propose a 30-day notice and the ability for Customer to object on reasonable grounds; Redwood will maintain a current subprocessor list in the customer console and provide evidence of subprocessors on request (certificate/stamped agreement).

4) KMS / Encryption: we can commit to BYOK for Dedicated/Private and HSM-backed key storage for Hosted EU-region. Suggested evidence list: SOC2 report excerpt, KMS rotation logs for the last 90 days, and a short architecture diagram. We cannot accept unlimited audit access to HSMs; evidence will be delivered via redacted operational logs and attestation.

I included inline edits for the indemnity/limitation section to reflect the SCCs interplay. If HealthBridge requires more prescriptive technical controls, that will push the conversation toward Dedicated/Private.

Attachments: DPA_markup_LB.docx

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Laura / Stephanie — thanks for the quick turnaround and the suggested language. A couple of follow-ups from our compliance team before we lock the call:
- The 30-day subprocessor notification window is reasonable but our team asked whether objections would be considered binding (we prefer ability to block for a short list of critical subprocessors). Can Redwood provide an example objection process and an expected SLA for remediation?
- For the Transfer Addendum: we'd like a short template that lists transfer routes (EU->US east, EU->APAC) with a checkbox model so procurement can accept route-specific assurances rather than re-negotiating the whole DPA each time.
- KMS evidence: the compliance team needs a sample KMS rotation log and an example attestation format.

Tom from procurement will own the order form residency clause if we need it. We're aiming to complete legal review by end of July. Can Redwood share the DocuSign envelope when you kick off signature?

Best,
Anika

Decisions agreed (draft):
- Role mapping: Redwood = Processor for API inference; Customer = Controller. Telemetry/usage metrics explicitly excluded from "Customer Data". (Owner: Laura — provide final clause)
- SCCs: Parties will rely on EU Commission SCCs and use a Transfer Addendum for route-specific mitigations. (Owner: Laura / Aditya — produce Transfer Addendum template)
- Subprocessor window: 30-day notice; HealthBridge can object on reasonable grounds with a documented remediation SLA. (Owner: Laura to draft objection flow; Owner: Ben to coordinate commercial exception if needed)
- KMS: BYOK for Dedicated/Private; HSM-backed KMS in EU for Hosted (evidence bundle: sample rotation log + attestation). (Owner: Aditya to prepare evidence packet)
- Order Form residency: Tom to confirm whether dataset X must be EU-only; if yes, we will add a residency SLO to the Order Form and nominal surcharge. (Owner: Tom)

- Laura: final DPA markup and Transfer Addendum template by 2027-07-22
- Aditya: KMS evidence packet (sample log + attestation) by 2027-07-22
- Ben / Stephanie: schedule tech/legal call for 2027-07-28 (30 min) and prepare Order Form draft if residency SLO is needed
- Tom / Anika: confirm dataset residency requirement by 2027-07-21
